title: A failed seek leaves the seek hold set. The deck can stay "playing" and silent.
comment:
**A failed seek leaves the seek hold set. The deck can stay "playing" and silent.**

`Engine::apply` sets `seeking[i]` to the ring epoch when it issues a seek. `progress` clears the hold only when `reader.epoch()` changes. `Producer::seek` in `deck_play.rs` opens a new epoch only after it decodes the first block. If `stream.change` or the prime decode fails, it calls `ring.end()` on the old epoch and returns `Seeked { ok: false }`. The engine never receives that result, because it only reaches the C log.

After that failure, the hold stays `Some` until the next load. These effects follow:
- `set_position_ms` is never called again.
- `finish_playback` is never reached, because it sits behind `seeking[i].is_none()`.
- `playing[i]` stays true once the old epoch drains.
- The Play LED stays on.
- Rendering is silent.

Trigger: a read error during a seek, such as card removal, or a decoder that rejects the target. Release the hold when the reader's current epoch has ended and drained, so the existing end-of-track path can run.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-            if self.seeking[i].is_some_and(|epoch| reader.epoch() != epoch) {
+            let drained = reader.ended(&RINGS[i]) && reader.buffered(&RINGS[i]) == 0;
+            if self.seeking[i].is_some_and(|epoch| reader.epoch() != epoch || drained) {
                 self.seeking[i] = None;
             }
```
</details>

Check this against a seek that starts after a track has ended. The producer then opens a new epoch on its next poll, so the hold may release one block early.
